extracted.intended_audience: readers of The Art of Computer Programming Volume 2 and people submitting errata or suggestions to Donald Knuth (editors/publishers, TAOCP readers)
extracted.subtask_description: Authoritative errata/change-policy document for The Art of Computer Programming, Volume 2: it defines categories of changes (bugs, amendments, improvements, plans), explains formatting/semantics, describes scope of updates, and gives instructions for submitting corrections and printing options.

rubrics_metrics.name: bugonpage (error corrections)
rubrics_metrics.description: "\bugonpage" introduces the correction of an error; Technical or typographical errors (aka bugs) are the most critical items, so they are flagged with a `\thinspace{\manfnt x}\thinspace' preceding the page number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The date shown is the date on which the author was first told about the bug (the effective date on which the finder's fee is paid). Necessary corrections are indicated in a straightforward way (example: `$n$ \becomes $n+1$`). Bug entries are intended to be the most critical items.

rubrics_metrics.name: amendpage (amendments / new material)
rubrics_metrics.description: "\amendpage" introduces new material for future editions; Amendments to the text appear in the same format as bugs, but without the `\thinspace{\manfnt x}\thinspace'. These are things I wish I had known about or thought of when I wrote the original text, so I added them later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The date shown for an amendment is the date the new text was drafted. Amendments represent substantive additions or corrections intended for future editions (distinct from immediate bug fixes).

rubrics_metrics.name: improvepage (minor improvements)
rubrics_metrics.description: "\improvepage" introduces ameliorations of lesser importance; The fourth category consists of minor corrections or improvements that most readers don't want to know about, because they are so trivial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Items introduced by \improvepage are printed in smaller, slanted type and (unless the user selected the 'long form') do not appear in the hardcopy listing. The document notes: "You wouldn't even be seeing these items if you hadn't specifically chosen to print the complete errata list in all its gory details."

rubrics_metrics.name: planforpage (plans / author intentions)
rubrics_metrics.description: "\planforpage" introduces some of the author's half-baked intentions; Plans for the future represent a kind of item in which the author sketches intentions that he wasn't ready to flesh out further when written.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan items are written in slanted type and preceded by a series of dots leading to the date on which the plan was recorded in the author's files. They are explicitly presented as sketches rather than finished corrections or amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: formatting/typographic conventions for change entries
rubrics_metrics.description: Different change categories use distinct typographic conventions: bug entries show a black-triangle symbol before the page number; amend entries use the same layout without the triangle; plan entries are slanted and preceded by dots; improve entries use smaller, slanted type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These conventions determine how an entry appears in the errata listing and help readers immediately identify the severity/type of each change.

rubrics_metrics.name: date semantics for entries (finder's fee / draft date)
rubrics_metrics.description: The date shown for a bug is the date on which the author was first told about the bug and is the effective date on which the finder's fee is paid. For amendments the date is the date the new text was drafted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dates are formatted via the document's \date macro (converting yy.mm.dd. to 'dd Mon 19yy' etc.); readers should interpret the date as provenance information (when the author learned of or drafted the item).

rubrics_metrics.name: scope-of-update criteria for Volume 2
rubrics_metrics.description: The author believes the changes bring Volume 2 completely up to date in two respects: (1) All of the research problems in the previous edition—i.e., all exercises that were rated 46 and above—have received new ratings of 45 or less whenever a solution was learned; and in such cases the answer now refers to that solution. (2) All of the historical information about pioneering developments has been amended whenever new details have come to the author's attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This states the editorial standard used to decide what updates to include: solved high-rated exercises get rating changes and references to solutions; historical notes are corrected when new details arrive.

rubrics_metrics.name: submission/contact policy for errata and suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: Please let me know of any improvements that you think I ought to make. Send your comments either by snail mail to D. E. Knuth, Computer Science, Gates Building 1B, Stanford University, Stanford CA 94305-9015, or by email to taocp@cs.stanford.edu.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use email for book suggestions only—"all other correspondence is returned unread to the sender, or discarded, because I have no time to read ordinary email." The author will try to reply to such messages within a year of receipt. Current news and the long-form errata are posted on the TAOCP webpage.

rubrics_metrics.name: visibility and long-form errata availability
rubrics_metrics.description: A fuller set of miscellaneous minor corrections or improvements exists in the author's personal file but is not shown in the short printed list; if you really want to see all of the gory details, you can download the full list (the 'long form') from the TAOCP webpage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By default the published errata omits trivial improvepage items; readers desiring exhaustive detail should retrieve the long-form errata from the indicated webpage.

rubrics_metrics.name: TeX/printing instruction: put index on separate page
rubrics_metrics.description: To put the index on a separate page, run this with the command line: tex "\let\indexeject+ \input err2"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit production instruction for typesetting the errata document (how to cause an index-eject behavior when running TeX).

rubrics_metrics.name: \all flag controls inclusion of trivial items
rubrics_metrics.description: The document defines a flag: \newif\ifall; \alltrue means show the trivial items too.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This flag governs whether improvepage/minor items are included in the displayed list: if \all is true, trivial items appear; otherwise they are suppressed from the short form.
